purpose: Teach: 片道/肘/釘/売り物/割安/夏場/治す/肩こり

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 修学旅行、片道で電車かバスか、迷うね。
lines.en: The school trip — are we going by train or bus one way? Can't decide.
lines.style: Conversational opener, thinking out loud. Slight lilt upward on the question. Casual, inviting input. Light, not pressing.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 重い荷物、肘、当たって痛い。
lines.en: Your elbow keeps hitting my bag when it's this heavy. Ouch.
lines.style: Dry complaint wrapped in half-humor. Matter-of-fact delivery, no drama. Quick timing on the hit-pay-off. Slight wince in the voice.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 教室の机、釘、ちょっと飛び出てて、注意。
lines.en: The classroom desk has a nail poking out of it. Just a heads up.
lines.style: Understated warning, genuinely helpful. Steady, calm tone. Pause before the caution — making sure he's listening. No alarm, just practicality.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 文房具屋、新しい売り物、見たい。
lines.en: Oh, there's a new stationery shop. We should check it out.
lines.style: Genuine interest breaking through. Lighter attack, a spark of enthusiasm. Lean into 'should check it out' like it's a plan forming in real time.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: コンビニのおにぎり、割安パック、お得だよね。
lines.en: The conbini's rice ball packs are such a good deal right now.
lines.style: Upbeat observation, like sharing a small treasure. Warm, approving tone. Quick rhythm. Not serious — just genuinely pleased by finding value.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 夏場、塩分補給、忘れずに。
lines.en: Summer's coming — don't forget to keep your salt intake up.
lines.style: Practical advice delivered lightly, almost protective without being mothering. Even pacing. Casual concern that knows better than to make a fuss.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 昨夜、薬で熱、治すことできた。
lines.en: I got my fever down with meds last night. Finally.
lines.style: Relief evident but restrained. Quiet satisfaction on 'finally.' Slower pace — tiredness still lingering. Exhale at the end, like releasing tension.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.en: Your shoulders are killing you these days, aren't they?
lines.style: Wry observation mixed with actual concern. Knowing tone — she's noticed the tension. Quick, not dwelling. Closes with a soft check-in, not prying.
